analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, which is documentation only. The patch adds a v0.10.13 candidate section (Gemma 4 loop-exit-thinking guard, pair-setup stop handling) and the retained older release notes follow it. No executable code, configuration or protocol definitions changed, so no control is added, removed or weakened in the supplied evidence.

The units I examined are mostly older release-note text. They mention security-adjacent behavior that this PR did not change: SSD prefix cache TTL and maintenance (relevant to T-041, with the TTL and eviction behavior described as unchanged), cluster encrypted peer sums, App Attest re-registration, the add-on hold (TB-012) and the sandbox installer (TB-013). None of this is a new claim introduced by this diff. The changelog text keeps its existing caveats. It says TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged, and that charges still precede writes. It also says Qwen27 tensor-parallel and GLM serving qualification gates stay separate and that component tests do not establish release readiness. So it does not overclaim qualification (T-056).

The new 0.10.13 notes describe two runtime changes, #2040 (Gemma loop guard) and #2042 (pair stop semantics). Their code is not in the supplied units, so it cannot be assessed here. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the new section was not visible. Neither change touches the encryption, attestation or authorization paths from what is visible. A future pass reviewing the source for #2040 and #2042 should check that the thinking-close injection does not bypass the logprobs or tool-constraint gates, and that the stop handling does not weaken peer-acknowledgement semantics.

No findings.
